long_biography.plain_text:
Nusli Neville Wadia entered the family enterprise through Bombay Dyeing, joining its board before becoming joint managing director and, in 1977, chairman. The company belonged to an industrial group whose roots predated him by generations. His early responsibilities were therefore those of a successor and operator, not a founder, and centred on stewarding the established textiles business.

His chairmanship of Britannia Industries added a major food business to the family portfolio. He has also chaired Bombay Burmah and other group companies while professional executives manage day-to-day operations. Today he remains chairman of the Wadia Group and a non-executive promoter director at major listed companies. His record combines inherited ownership with long-term strategic expansion of a diversified portfolio.
